taylor: quick sanity-check run for weight-only INT8 on aurora-13b. compared bitsandbytes (bnb) load_in_8bit vs llm.int8 loader on our dev RTX6000. throwing raw numbers below, want opinions on rollout risk and perf knobs. @sara @omar

sara: nice. can you paste the exact commands and the eval harness you used? also which dataset (mmlu/commonsense/perplexity)?

 taylor: ran mmlu few-shot (the usual redwood/eval-mmlu subset), winogrande, and held-out perplexity on wiki-latest. commands:```
# bitsandbytes (bnb) load_in_8bit flow
python -c "from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained('redwood/aurora-13b', load_in_8bit=True, device_map='auto')
Tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('redwood/aurora-13b')
print('loaded bnb')"

# llm.int8 loader (example API)
python -c "from llm_int8 import load_8bit
model = load_8bit('redwood/aurora-13b', device='cuda')
print('loaded llm.int8')"
```

Used our eval harness: `python eval/run_eval.py --tasks mmlu,winogrande --batch 8 --temp 0.0 --seed 42 --prefix_cache true`

omar: good. what are the numbers?

 taylor: pasted summary (all numbers averaged over 3 runs):
- fp16 baseline: MMLU acc 48.2%, Winogrande acc 76.1%, perplexity 12.3, tokens/s (greedy) 220, peak VRAM 24G
- bnb weight-only int8: MMLU acc 46.7% (-1.5), Winogrande 75.0% (-1.1), perplexity 13.1 (+0.8), tokens/s 260 (+18%), peak VRAM ~9G
- llm.int8 (weight-only): MMLU acc 47.6% (-0.6), Winogrande 75.6% (-0.5), perplexity 12.6 (+0.3), tokens/s 200 (-9%), peak VRAM ~11G

liam: interesting — bnb gives the biggest compression and fastest throughput but the largest drop in closed-book accuracy. llm.int8 sits between perf and quality. did you look at answer drift (e.g., more hallucinations) or only accuracy?

 taylor: looked at top-1 token changes on a held set. bnb had higher token-delta early in generation (first 30 tokens) on QA prompts. qualitative failure modes: more truncation/shorter answers and occasionally wrong factual anchors. llm.int8 produced slightly more verbose answers similar to fp16.

 sara: do we know if bnb applied per-channel quant or symmetric quant? might be the scale handling on some layers causing drift. can you dump per-layer ranges?

 taylor: bnb uses 8-bit per-channel (optimised weight-only path) AFAIK; llm.int8 uses a different packing (nonlinear quant + scale calibration). i dumped blockwise max stats — will attach CSV to the ticket. quick glance: attention.out_proj and some MLP proj layers have highest dynamic range and worst delta correlation.

 eval-bot: quick eval summary uploaded to /evals/1769501234/ (MMLU/Winogrande/perp). small table: fp16:48.2 | bnb:46.7 | llm.int8:47.6. see artifact for per-layer norms.

 omar: thanks. two suggestions: (1) try calibration via KL-min or MSE sweep on a small calibration set (5k tokens) for bnb if supported, (2) run longer-context (2k tokens) generation to see KV cache sensitivity. int8 sometimes amplifies conditioning errors over long contexts.

 taylor: agreed. next steps I'm proposing:
- run bnb with 5k-token KL calibration (if available) and re-eval on mmlu + long-context QA
- run llm.int8 with different quantization seeds (some libs have nondet pack order)
- add a quick canary route in Redwood runtime: default -> llm.int8, fallback to fp16 for critical routes if accuracy regression > threshold (we can use rollout policy + eval hooks)

 liam: also try a mixed strategy: bnb for short-response routes (chatbot assistant quick replies) where latency wins, llm.int8 for retrieval/qa for fewer regressions. keep metric: tokens-per-dollar and answer-f1 on our sampled sets.

 sara: will help with automation to collect per-route evals and wire into Optimize suggestions.

 taylor: awesome. I'll kick off calibration runs and post updated numbers here. tagging @omar to review the long-context results when ready. :rocket:

 liam: :thumbsup:
